Implementation + test evidence (LOCAL). Final reconciliation pass 2026-10-27.

Changed: TelegramTransport.receiptFor derives the receipt tuple from the actual Bot API transport class plus the actual response — peer from response chat.id (a response with no chat leaves the destination UNVERIFIED; no echo of the requested chat), mediaType from the medium the response carries (no fallback to the asked-for type), idProtocol from the transport class ("bot_api"), and account from the response `from` identity when present, else the cached getMe bot identity (a response naming a different sender is reported as that sender, never hidden by ours). bot.taskReceipt is attestation-only and no longer infers idProtocol from the transport-name prefix nor peer from the request; the ledger notify path no longer fills a missing peer from chatKey. start_task persists expectedPeer/expectedAccount/expectedIdProtocol, and bot.runLedgerTask delivers the result medium ONLY to an explicit different expectedPeer via an authorised reachable transport, or throws a precise "no reachable transport ... refusing to send to the origin" blocker without any wrong-peer send. API ack / readback / human view remain distinct. Also: the expectedPeer tool description no longer offers a Saved Messages chat id — the Bot API cannot address Saved Messages, and the description now requires an already-authorised reachable bot chat (e.g. "telegram:123456") and states Saved Messages needs a separately authorised account/protocol route (no new route, no access widening).

title: Auto-compaction for agent sessions (percent threshold, ctx.compact, bounded resume)
description:
## Problem
Agent sessions grow past every model's real limit before pi's native auto-compaction fires.

Evidence (2026-10-05): mentalhealthtech's session reached ~512k tokens.
- Pi triggers at `contextTokens > contextWindow - reserveTokens`.
- pibot declares `ollama/glm-5.3-flash:cloud` contextWindow = 1048576, so the trigger sits at ~1.03M.
- The cascade then switched to `openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` (real limit 163840) and every call failed:
  `400 ... requested about 548921 tokens (512069 of text input)`.
- The same runaway run produced the false "finished that turn without a reply" warnings.

pibot builds sessions with `SettingsManager.inMemory({})` and its own `DefaultResourceLoader`,
so `pi install` into `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` never reaches pibot agents.

## Decisions (owner, 2026-10-05)
1. Implement as a pibot plugin modelled on npm:pi-auto-compact (percent threshold + `ctx.compact()`).
2. Trigger = percent of the **active model's declared** context window (upstream parity), configurable.
3. Auto-resume: **yes** - one bounded follow-up after a compaction that interrupted an unfinished turn.

## Design
`src/plugins/auto-compact-plugin.ts` -> `autoCompactPlugin(deps): InlineExtension`, wired in
`agent-manager.ts` next to the capability extensions (host-level, so every agent is protected
without editing private per-agent manifests).

- `input` (only when `event.streamingBehavior === undefined`, i.e. the agent is idle):
  project `usage.tokens + estimateTokens(new message)`; at/over threshold -> `ctx.compact()` and
  await completion before letting the prompt through. No abort, no resume needed.
- `turn_end` (agent mid-run): at/over threshold -> `ctx.compact()` (aborts the run) then queue
  exactly one `[compaction-resume]` follow-up so the interrupted work continues.
  Re-arms only after usage falls back under the threshold.
- Never fail-closed: a hard compaction failure is logged and the prompt proceeds, because
  dropping the owner's message silently is the exact failure mode this work is fixing.
- Config: `<dataDir>/auto-compact.json` `{ "enabled": true, "threshold": 78 }`, hot-read.
- All decisions logged to the agent EventLog (`compaction: ...`).

## Residual risk (accepted, needs owner follow-up)
With glm declaring 1M, a 78% threshold is ~817k - still above the 163k real limit of cascade peers.
Correcting the declared `contextWindow` for the ollama models in `~/.pi/agent/models.json`
(1M -> realistic) is what makes the trigger fire in time.

## Tests
- no compaction while under threshold; skips queued (streamingBehavior) prompts
- compacts + awaits at/over threshold on an idle prompt
- turn_end compaction queues exactly one resume; no resume when the turn ended with a final answer
- resume re-arms only after usage drops back under threshold
- soft error ("Nothing to compact") does not drop the prompt; hard error logs and continues
- config file parsed, clamped, hot-reloaded
close_reason: Closed

Independent confirmation + today's occurrence (cross-check of the 16:44 flow review). This is not theoretical: data/daemon.log (lines ~220-266) shows a DNS outage (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND api.telegram.org) where outbound sends died silently:

title: Telegram push: mismatched HTML entities drop the whole message
description: Sep 18: a bot push to the owner chat (161427550) failed with 400 Bad Request: can't parse entities: Unmatched end tag at byte offset 604, expected "", found "". The message was lost — same user-visible symptom as the silent-turn bug. Cause: toTelegramHtml() in src/transports/telegram.ts runs three sequential regex passes over the escaped text (**bold**, *italic*, `code`). Sequential passes can cross tags when delimiters overlap (e.g. `a *b` c*), producing HTML Telegram refuses. push() then has no fallback: the sendMessage call throws and nothing arrives. Fix: single-pass, stack-disciplined conversion that cannot emit crossed tags, plus a plain-text degrade path so a formatting rejection never costs the message.

title: Jev shadow evaluation for skill evolution
description:
## Goal
Evaluate Jev as a typed, advisory judge in PiBot's existing skill self-evolution loop while the current 1-5 judge and deterministic promotion policy remain authoritative.

## Scope
- Build consented, independent replay cases from eligible staged or historical skills, with verified baseline and candidate versions and blinded human labels.
- Add a default-off, per-agent, provider/data-scoped shadow observer at the probe/judge boundary. Bound input, calls, queue, timeout, and metadata retention; keep private text out of logs.
- Compare Jev and current-judge outcomes with human labels, including disagreements, severe misses, false reviews, unavailable results, latency, and cost.
- Return a decision report for owner review before any active gate or promotion-policy change.

## Non-goals
No replacement of the current judge, no Jev promotion/veto, no live deployment, and no link-triage changes under this epic.

## Success Criteria
Shadow outcomes cannot change scores, staging, promotion, announcements, or backlog closure; boundary tests cover success and all fallback classes. Replay provenance and data permission are documented. The report states evidence and limitations. Any active gate requires a separate approved decision.

## Spec
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-25-jev-evolution-shadow-evaluation.md

- src/core/evolution.ts — judge() may return { score, parse } (a fallback 3 is now distinguishable from a parsed one; bare numbers still work); snapshot captured after each probe reply exists; observe() never awaited; promoted/staged recorded as metadata. Current 1-5 judge, avg>=4 rule, gates, staging, announcements and backlog closure untouched.
- src/core/jev-replay.ts — selection refuses proposer-authored criteria, unprovenanced patch baselines and disallowed data classes; deterministic blinded A/B; verdicts naming false passes/false reviews; repeat stability; limitation-stating report.
- Tests: 22 shadow + 9 boundary + 13 replay. Boundary suite pins that success / misses_required disagreement / timeout / invalid output / provider denial each leave score, staging, promotion, announcement and backlog closure byte-identical to a no-shadow control. Full suite 777 green, tsc clean.
- Docs: docs/evolution-pipeline.md shadow section; plan + execution ledger in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-25-jev-evolution-shadow-evaluation.md.

REMAINING (owner)
1. Author the replay set: owner-reviewed tasks/criteria and BLINDED human labels for eligible staged/historical candidates. Stratify create/patch, prior high/low scores, risky/ordinary. Exclude anything outside the approved data scope. Code refuses to accept proposer-authored criteria by construction.

3. Wire the observer in index.ts and set the per-agent flag — deliberately NOT done: the spec lists live deployment as out of scope, and the epic's non-goals exclude it.

title: No wall-clock cap on a user turn — a hung model leaves the owner in silence
description:
turnWithCascade awaits session.prompt(...) with no timeout. PIBOT_TG_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS (30s) bounds individual Telegram API calls only; MAX_TURN_MODELS=5 bounds model RETRIES, not duration. TelegramTransport.WORK_MAX_MS=180_000 stops the typing/reaction cycle but nothing else.

Consequence: a hung or endlessly streaming model call = no reply, no error, no dead letter, no notice, no event — the same invisible-silence class as pibot-z95.5/d1f4046, and the 180s marker stop removes the last visual hint.

The review's M2 covers only agentTurn (delegated) timeouts, not the owner-facing path.

Fix sketch: race the turn against a bounded wall clock (e.g. PIBOT_TURN_TIMEOUT_MS, default 10-15m) -> abort the session prompt, log a 'system' event, and push an honest notice ('turn exceeded <N>m and was stopped; ask again or /new'). Also surface the elapsed time in /status while a turn is in flight.

title: [bug] Duplicate guard silently drops legitimate identical replies (<30s)
description:
TelegramDuplicateGuard is applied to EVERY push, not just proactive sends: push() calls shouldSend(chatId, JSON({text,card})) and returns early on a match inside DUPLICATE_WINDOW_MS (30s), leaving only a console.warn. Two identical replies to one chat within 30s => the second never arrives and the owner sees silence.

Evidence (already happened): data/daemon.log.old:1549 region — '[telegram] <- /cancel' twice, then 'suppressed duplicate send to chat 161427550'; the second /cancel got no reply. One more occurrence in data/daemon.log. Total 2 in log history, so rare but a genuine silent-drop path of exactly the class fixed in d1f4046.

The pibot-dev full-flow review (reports/flow-review-2026-09-18.md) lists the duplicate guard under 'verified-good' — disagree: it should not apply to replies to a user turn.

Fix sketch: skip the guard for user-turn replies (pass an explicit 'userFacing: true'/skipDedupe flag from onSessionEvent + promptAgent), or key the guard on turn identity (incoming message id) instead of payload equality. Keep it for proactive/heartbeat pushes.
close_reason: Fixed in 9e0bb3b: PushOptions.dedupeKey carries the turn's identity (chat + incoming message id), so identical answers to two different messages both send while an accidental double-fire of the same turn is still suppressed. Proactive pushes keep payload dedupe. 3 transport tests. Deployed 17:09, harness 4/4.

title: media: complete safe Telegram audio round-trip
description: Complete the Telegram speech pipeline without automatic or proactive audio. Inbound: support native voice, audio, video_note, and validated audio documents; download within Telegram and project limits, extract only the audio track from video notes locally, transcribe, and route the transcript through the invoking transport and current or bound agent exactly like a user turn. Outbound: add an agent-scoped opt-in speech capability with provider abstraction, private generated artifacts, and transport methods for Telegram voice messages and music-player audio. Local generation is the default; external TTS or STT is disabled unless explicitly configured and permitted for that agent. Reuse the existing rate limit and duplicate guard; never attach speech generation to heartbeat, schedules, replay, or automatic reply conversion. Coordinate retention with pibot-7bo.
design: Phase 1 hardens ingestion: extend IncomingMedia for video_note, accept audio documents only after MIME and media probing, use execFile-based ffmpeg extraction with duration, byte, timeout, and output limits, and resolve the target agent before choosing STT policy. Keep transcripts as user content, not system instructions, and preserve pending-question behavior. Phase 2 adds Telegram sendVoice and sendAudio adapters plus an agent-scoped speech capability with separate generate and send actions targeting only the invoking chat. Use a local macOS say plus ffmpeg adapter first behind a provider interface; generated voice output is OGG Opus or another Telegram-supported voice format, while audio output is MP3 or M4A. Phase 3 adds optional external adapters such as OpenAI, Groq Orpheus, or ElevenLabs with secret presence checks, per-agent provider allowlists, no discovery calls, and explicit owner intent for paid or external generation. Artifacts and downloads stay outside Git with owner-only permissions and bounded retention; operational events contain metadata only, never transcript or audio content.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Focused tests cover message:voice, message:audio, message:video_note, and valid or invalid audio documents, including size, duration, missing-audio-track, malformed-media, timeout, and download failure cases. 2. Video-note audio is extracted locally with argument-safe process execution and the transcript reaches only the agent bound to the invoking bot or selected in that exact chat. 3. Pending questions can be answered by all supported speech inputs; spoken slash commands never become host commands accidentally. 4. STT policy is local-first and external transcription occurs only when that provider is configured and allowed for the resolved agent; tests prove no external call during discovery or when disallowed. 5. An opt-in agent capability can generate locally and send either Telegram voice via sendVoice or audio via sendAudio to the invoking chat only; format and 50 MB Telegram upload constraints are validated. 6. Audio delivery uses the existing per-chat queue, flood control, retry-after handling, and duplicate suppression, and has no heartbeat, scheduler, replay, or automatic reply hook. 7. Downloaded and generated files use private directories and 0600 files, filenames do not expose raw chat identifiers, and retention or immediate cleanup is enforced with pibot-7bo. 8. Logs and events record provider, format, duration, latency, outcome, and safe error category only; they never record audio bytes, transcript text, generated speech text, secrets, or credentials. 9. README documents supported Telegram types, local and external provider policy, privacy and retention, and opt-in behavior.
notes: Phase 1 implemented in working tree: Telegram video_note and validated audio documents; private opaque downloads with 20 MB and duration limits; ffprobe validation and bounded ffmpeg audio-only extraction; source containment and symlink rejection; immediate speech-media cleanup; target agent resolved before STT; local-first STT with external Groq denied unless explicitly listed and allowExternalStt is true in that agent speech policy; safe user-facing errors. Verification: typecheck passes and full Vitest 319/319 passes. No runtime restart, Telegram send, external STT, or paid call performed. Phase 2 local-only TTS remains in progress.
close_reason: Implemented both phases in the working tree: safe bounded video-note/audio-document ingestion with agent-scoped local-first STT policy, plus opt-in local-only speech generation and invoking-chat Telegram voice/audio delivery. Full Vitest 335/335, typecheck, diff-check, and real local say/ffmpeg OGG+M4A smoke pass. No external API call, Telegram send, restart, commit, or deploy performed.

title: Encrypt the dashboard session stores (web-auth-secret, web-sessions.json)
description:
Two credential files remain plaintext outside the sops stores, both in data/ (0600, gitignored):

title: Dead-letter cap silently breaks the 'your message is saved' promise

During a long multi-provider outage the oldest queued owner messages are therefore discarded after a promise that they were kept. Noted only as a parenthetical in the pibot-dev review's L8.

Fix sketch: when truncating, events.log a 'system' entry naming how many queued messages were dropped, and push one owner notice ('N older queued messages were dropped after the queue hit its 100-message cap'). Consider raising the cap or spilling to a file rather than dropping user text.

title: Reply media attachments fail silently (no event, no notice)

A failed attachment therefore leaves the text reply without its file and leaves only a console line — no event-log entry, no owner-visible signal — while the sibling case (transport has no sendMedia) is explicitly event-logged ('media dropped: ...') after the Sep 16 creator incident.

Fix sketch: mirror the existing 'media dropped' handling on the failure path: events.log(agentId, 'system', 'media send failed: <source> — <error>') and append one short notice to the already-sent text (or a follow-up line) so the owner knows a file was missing.
